newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK visa rules to be largely unchanged after handover.
newsitem.headline: HK visa rules to be largely unchanged after handover.

text.p: Hong Kong visa requirements for most foreigners will be largely unchanged after China takes over the colony from Britain next week, but there will be some tightening for Britons, immigration officials said on Friday.
"Basically the present policy will not change," Sunny Ho, a spokesman for the Immigration Department, told Reuters in response to inquiries.

The present visa system for foreigners will remain except for some adjustments with Thailand, Ho said. Hong Kong is prepared to increase the length of the visa-free period for Thai tourists to one month from 14 days.
"Everything stays unchanged unless there has been an announcement of changes," he said.
At present, foreigners coming to Hong Kong to work, study, settle or set up a business need a visa.
As for tourists, only nationals from 35 countries and stateless people need a visa. Other foreigners have visa-free access for visits of varying lengths from seven days to six months.
In general the visa requirement for each country will remain the same under the Chinese as under British rule, Ho said.
"At present nationals of most foreign countries can visit Hong Kong visa-free. This liberal visa policy will continue after 1 July, 1997," an Immigration Deparment spokesman said.
British citizens however face a major change.
Under colonial rule, Britons were able to stay for any purpose for up to a year. A legion of British backpackers took advantage of this to stay back in Hong Kong and work.
But from July 1, the visa-free period for British tourists will be shortened to six months. Any Briton wanting to work, study or settle in Hong Kong will need a visa.

All Chinese diplomatic and consular missions are now accepting visa applications for entry to Hong Kong from July 1. Applicants can also submit visa applications to the Immigration Department themselves, or through sponsors in Hong Kong.
